title: Roller Coaster
summary: Build a gravity-driven track that delivers a ball to the finish line at a target time, and understand the scoring function well enough to design against it.
objectives: Account for a run using gravitational potential energy, rolling kinetic energy and friction losses.
Design for a target time revealed on competition day rather than for the fastest possible run.
Earn the discretionary points the scoring function offers for loop height and elevators.
Test and calibrate so a practised run repeats within a fraction of a second.
Present a device that passes inspection and answer a judge's questions about it.

units.title: The Event and the Score
units.summary: In a build event the scoring function is the design brief. Read it first, because it says plainly where the points are and which instincts to distrust.
objectives: State every term of the run score and which are under the team's control before the tournament.
Explain why a smaller device and a slower run can both raise the score.

lessons.title: Reading the Scoring Function as a Design Brief
lessons.objective: Break the run score into its size, time, elevator and loop terms and decide where the next hour of build time is best spent.

lessons.title: Constraints, Impound, and Staying Legal
lessons.objective: Check a device against the size envelope, the gravity-only propulsion rule and the visibility requirement before it is ever impounded.

units.title: Energy on a Gravity Track
units.summary: Height is the only fuel the device gets. Everything after the release is that energy being spent.
objectives: Convert gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy along a path.
Account for the energy that friction and rolling resistance remove.

lessons.title: From Height to Speed: Potential and Kinetic Energy
lessons.objective: Compute the speed a sphere reaches after a drop and explain why the path shape does not change that speed, only the time taken to reach it.

lessons.title: Where the Energy Goes: Friction and Rolling Resistance
lessons.objective: Distinguish sliding friction from rolling resistance and predict how surface and ball choice change the energy left at the finish.

lessons.title: Rolling, Not Sliding: Why the Ball Matters
lessons.objective: Explain how a rolling sphere stores energy in rotation, and predict how diameter, mass and material change travel time.

units.title: Hitting the Target Time
units.summary: The target time is revealed on the day, so the device has to be tunable rather than fast.
objectives: Extend or shorten a run time predictably without rebuilding the track.
Design adjustment mechanisms that survive the setup period.

lessons.title: Controlling Run Time: Path Length, Slope, and Speed
lessons.objective: Use gentle gradients, added path length and controlled speed regulation to place a run inside the target window.

lessons.title: Tunable Design and Calibration
lessons.objective: Build adjustable elements and a calibration table so a revealed target time becomes a setting rather than a problem.

units.title: Loops and Elevators
units.summary: These are the optional point sources, and each is a physics problem with a legality condition attached.
objectives: Design a loop the ball completes while staying in contact with the track.
Build lever-based elevators that raise the sphere and keep it on the track.

lessons.title: Loop Physics: Staying on the Track at the Top
lessons.objective: Use centripetal force to find the minimum speed at the top of a loop, and measure loop height from the point of intersection.

lessons.title: Elevators: Levers, Wheel and Axle, and Pulleys
lessons.objective: Build a first-class-lever elevator and a second-class-lever elevator with a pulley, and explain why each runs at a mechanical advantage below one.

units.title: Build, Test, and Compete
units.summary: A device that works once is not finished; the score comes from the better of two runs on an unfamiliar table.
objectives: Build a rigid, transportable track whose behaviour does not change between venues.
Run a testing programme that produces a reliable second run.

lessons.title: Construction, Transport, and the Automatic Stop
lessons.objective: Build for rigidity and repeatability, and design an automatic stopping mechanism that acts after the finish line.

lessons.title: A Testing Programme and Competition Day
lessons.objective: Plan a testing programme that records every run, and rehearse setup, release and the judge's questions.
